english.title: Keep / confine bird in small cage / receptacle
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), kept or confined

(A)_[a bird,]_
(B)_[birds,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY..),

(C)_[in a cage]_
(D)_[in a receptacle]_

which was not sufficient in height, length or breadth to permit the

(E)_[bird to stretch its]_
(F)_[birds to stretch their]_

wings freely
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 8(1) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
keep/confine bird(s)
in a cage/receptacle
which was not sufficient in height/length/breadth
to permit the bird(s)
to stretch its wings freely

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 8(2) for exceptions.
(ii) Applies to domestic and wild birds.
(iii) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(iv) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(v) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one bird is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each bird (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation
